---
title: "Quasi-Poisson regression"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Quasi-Poisson regression keeps the Poisson mean function but allows

$$
\operatorname{Var}[Y_i\mid\mathbf x_i]=\phi\mu_i.
$$

It thus changes uncertainty, not fitted means. The Nettle data show the distinction directly.

```{r}
#| label: load-and-fit-quasi
#| echo: true
path <- "data/nettle/nettle-1999-climate.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  nettle <- read.csv(path)
} else {
  url <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bodowinter/",
                "applied_statistics_book_data/master/nettle_1999_climate.csv")
  source_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  download.file(url, source_file, mode = "wb")
  stopifnot(digest::digest(source_file, "sha256", file = TRUE, serialize = FALSE) ==
    "3c5abfbec7b2132a9b81ee9a178cbd5559426578032b60c6c4ad74046898793b")
  raw <- read.csv(source_file)
  nettle <- data.frame(country = raw$Country, log10_population = raw$Population,
    log10_area_km2 = raw$Area, log_area_km2 = log(10) * raw$Area,
    mean_growing_season_months = raw$MGS, language_count = as.integer(raw$Langs))
}
formula <- language_count ~ mean_growing_season_months + offset(log_area_km2)
poisson_fit <- glm(formula, poisson(), nettle)
quasi_fit <- glm(formula, quasipoisson(), nettle)
stopifnot(max(abs(fitted(poisson_fit) - fitted(quasi_fit))) < 1e-8)
data.frame(
  model = c("Poisson", "quasi-Poisson"),
  mgs_estimate = c(coef(poisson_fit)[[2L]], coef(quasi_fit)[[2L]]),
  mgs_standard_error = c(summary(poisson_fit)$coefficients[2L, 2L],
                         summary(quasi_fit)$coefficients[2L, 2L]),
  dispersion = c(1, summary(quasi_fit)$dispersion)
)
```

The MGS coefficient and every fitted rate are identical, while the standard error expands from `r round(summary(poisson_fit)$coefficients[2L, 2L], 4)` to `r round(summary(quasi_fit)$coefficients[2L, 2L], 4)`. The estimated dispersion is `r round(summary(quasi_fit)$dispersion, 2)`.

```{r}
#| label: plot-quasi-shared-fit
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
nettle$rate <- nettle$language_count / exp(nettle$log_area_km2)
grid <- data.frame(mean_growing_season_months =
  seq(min(nettle$mean_growing_season_months),
      max(nettle$mean_growing_season_months), length.out = 200L))
grid$rate <- exp(coef(quasi_fit)[[1L]] + coef(quasi_fit)[[2L]] *
                   grid$mean_growing_season_months)
ggplot(nettle, aes(mean_growing_season_months, rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) + geom_line(data = grid, color = "#1F5A85", linewidth = .8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Mean growing season (months)", y = "Languages per square kilometer") +
  theme_classic()
```

Quasi-likelihood does not define a complete probability mass function, so ordinary likelihood comparisons such as AIC are unavailable. It repairs the variance used for standard errors, not omitted structure, country dependence, or the exposure assumption.
